assessment.nobel_worthiness: A rare case of a theoretical prediction (flat bands at a magic twist angle) followed by an experimental discovery (correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018) that opened a new field of tunable correlated and topological matter. The originality and clarity of the central idea are high, and the field it created is very large.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. This is a natural three-way split. Other contributors (for example Cao, Fatemi, Dean and Young, or Santos and Lopes dos Santos) are not in the credited set and are not proposed here.
assessment.maturity: Seven or more years of independent confirmation by many groups, with a stable interpretation of the flat-band origin. The microscopic nature of the superconductivity remains debated, but the discovery itself is secure and timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should recognise the prediction, the experiment, or both, and how to treat parallel twistronics work that is not in the credited names.
Pairing mechanism of the superconducting phase is still unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and later the TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 associations, is a discovery of a new window on the cosmos made by an instrument of a new kind. The discovery stands at the centre of the case, and it points to cosmic-ray accelerators that remain unidentified.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual driver of IceCube and Karle was central to the detector and early analysis, so a two-person configuration is credible. The IceCube collaboration is very large, and others (for example early AMANDA and DUMAND pioneers) are not in the credited names, which leaves a real allocation question.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed by independent analyses and channels. Source identification is more recent and the evidence for individual sources is at moderate significance, so the discovery is mature while the source picture is still developing.
uncertainties: Credit within a large collaboration and relative to DUMAND, AMANDA and Baikal pioneers.
Individual source associations are not yet at overwhelming significance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and three-dimensional topological insulators reshaped how condensed matter is classified, with a clear, concrete discovery: protected edge and surface states. The concept has deep ties to mathematics and field theory, and its influence is broad.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) provided the theoretical foundation and Molenkamp's HgTe experiment gave the first observation of the quantum spin Hall state. Hasan's ARPES work established three-dimensional topological insulators experimentally. The decisive theory by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (the HgTe proposal) is not among the credited names, and Mele's role is substantial, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Well over a decade of independent confirmation in many materials, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is on time and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Missing or deceased contributors, and the Kane-Mele versus Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang priority, complicate a three-person split.
Whether the three-dimensional and two-dimensional discoveries should be recognised together.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength idea, has taken timekeeping to the 10^-18 level and enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic redshift across millimetres and a possible redefinition of the second. The invention is original, precise and has lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the experimental performance. This is a clean two-person attribution, though other clock groups (ion clocks, Wineland's earlier recognition) form part of the landscape.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many laboratories with steady improvements, and the interpretation is stable. Redefinition of the second is pending, so the timing is good rather than premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with Ye's other credited candidates and the extent to which this is metrology rather than a discovery in nature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations give a standard ruler imprinted by early-universe sound waves and detected in galaxy clustering. They provide one of the cleanest probes of the expansion history and dark energy, which is a discovery directly relevant to questions I care about.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections came from SDSS (Eisenstein) and 2dFGRS (Cole and the 2dF team); I choose these two as the observational pair. Peacock led much 2dF clustering work. Theoretical antecedents (Peebles and Yu, Sunyaev and Zeldovich) are not in the credited set and complicate the story.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed repeatedly by BOSS, eBOSS and DESI, with consistent results. DESI's recent hints of evolving dark energy are new, but the BAO measurement itself is robust.
uncertainties: Large survey collaborations and theoretical precursors make the attribution contestable.
Implications for dark energy are still in flux, though the measurement is not.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned the cosmic microwave background into a precision tool, fixing the age, geometry and composition of the universe and providing key evidence for the standard cosmological model. Its impact is large, although it is an instrument and survey achievement building on an existing Nobel-recognised discovery of anisotropy.
assessment.attribution: Bennett was the principal investigator, Page a leading experimentalist and instrument builder, and Spergel the leading analyst. This is a plausible trio, though the WMAP team was large and the Planck mission and COBE (already recognised) overlap conceptually.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and superseded in precision by Planck; the interpretation is stable. The risk is that the prize would look like a redundant recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 and 2019 cosmology prizes reduces novelty.
Credit among many WMAP team members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation addresses the horizon, flatness and structure-origin problems, and its prediction of a nearly scale-invariant spectrum of primordial fluctuations matches the data. It is conceptually profound, but as a theorist I note that the underlying mechanism is not identified and primordial gravitational waves have not been detected.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the original scenario, Linde the new and chaotic versions that make it viable, and Mukhanov the quantum origin of perturbations. Starobinsky and Sato are not in the credited set, which makes any fair configuration questionable.
assessment.maturity: Observational support from CMB spectra and flatness is strong but indirect. The absence of B-mode detection and the lack of a unique model make recognition arguably premature for a prize centred on discoveries.
uncertainties: No direct detection of primordial gravitational waves, and the model space is large.
Priority questions involving Starobinsky and others outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Direct horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are a striking observational discovery, giving the first visual evidence of a black-hole shadow and testing general relativity in the strong-field regime. The result is clear, though much of the underlying physics was already recognised in 2020.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the global array and Moran contributed decisive VLBI development. The enormous collaboration makes any three-person selection arbitrary to some degree.
assessment.maturity: Independent imaging epochs and two sources give good consistency, but the interpretation of polarisation and spin remains under development. It is timely but not yet fully mature.
uncertainties: Collaboration size and the arbitrariness of a three-person limit.
